title.en: I used to: what was so

rule.sl:
**used to** + osnovna oblika za to, kar je bilo in zdaj ni več, za vse osebe enako: **I used to live in Leeds.** (Nekoč sem živel{m:|f:a} v Leedsu.) **There used to be a shop by the bridge.** Lahko je stanje ali navada: **Old Wilf used to walk to school.**

Zanikano: **I didn't use to like tea.** Vprašanje: **Did you use to live here?** **Where did you use to work?** Za did je use: ljudje pišejo tudi *didn't used to*, slišati je enako; v pisanju je **didn't use to**. Tudi **never used to** in, bolj uradno, **used not to**.

Ljudje pišejo tudi *I use to*; v pisanju je **I used to**. Sedanjika nima: zdaj je **I usually walk**.

Kdaj, kolikokrat, koliko časa: past simple. **I lived in Leeds for five years.** **We went to Keswick last Tuesday.** **used to** pove le, da je bilo tako: **We used to go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (Tudi **We went** je tu prav.)

Da je mimo: **I don't live there any more.** Da še traja: **I still walk.**
rule.de:
**used to** + Grundform für das, was früher so war und jetzt nicht mehr ist, für alle Personen gleich: **I used to live in Leeds.** (Früher habe ich in Leeds gewohnt.) **There used to be a shop by the bridge.** Ein Zustand oder eine Gewohnheit: **Old Wilf used to walk to school.**

Verneint: **I didn't use to like tea.** Frage: **Did you use to live here?** **Where did you use to work?** Nach did steht use: Man schreibt auch *didn't used to*, es klingt gleich; geschrieben steht **didn't use to**. Auch **never used to** und, förmlicher, **used not to**.

Man schreibt auch *I use to*; geschrieben steht **I used to**. Eine Gegenwart hat es nicht: jetzt **I usually walk**.

Wann, wie oft, wie lange: past simple. **I lived in Leeds for five years.** **We went to Keswick last Tuesday.** **used to** sagt nur, dass es so war: **We used to go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (Auch **We went** stimmt hier.)

Dass es vorbei ist: **I don't live there any more.** Dass es noch gilt: **I still walk.**
rule.it:
**used to** + la forma base per ciò che era così e adesso non lo è più, uguale per tutte le persone: **I used to live in Leeds.** (Una volta abitavo a Leeds.) **There used to be a shop by the bridge.** Uno stato o un'abitudine: **Old Wilf used to walk to school.**

Negativo: **I didn't use to like tea.** Domanda: **Did you use to live here?** **Where did you use to work?** Dopo did si scrive use: si scrive anche *didn't used to*, il suono è lo stesso; per iscritto **didn't use to**. Anche **never used to** e, più formale, **used not to**.

Si scrive anche *I use to*; per iscritto **I used to**. Non ha il presente: adesso **I usually walk**.

Quando, quante volte, quanto tempo: past simple. **I lived in Leeds for five years.** **We went to Keswick last Tuesday.** **used to** dice solo che era così: **We used to go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (Anche **We went** qui è giusto.)

Per dire che è finito: **I don't live there any more.** Che dura ancora: **I still walk.**
rule.en:
**used to** + the base form for what was so and isn't now, the same for every person: **I used to live in Leeds.** **There used to be a shop by the bridge.** A state or a habit: **Old Wilf used to walk to school.**

No: **I didn't use to like tea.** To ask: **Did you use to live here?** **Where did you use to work?** After did it's use: people also write *didn't used to*, and it sounds the same; writing wants **didn't use to**. Also **never used to** and, more formal, **used not to**.

People also write *I use to*; writing wants **I used to**. It has no present: now it's **I usually walk**.

When, how many times, how long: the past simple. **I lived in Leeds for five years.** **We went to Keswick last Tuesday.** **used to** only says it was so: **We used to go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (**We went** is right here too.)

To say it's over: **I don't live there any more.** That it isn't: **I still walk.**

tip.sl: 💡 Slovenščina reče *nekoč*, *včasih* in preteklik, angleščina **used to** + osnovna oblika.
tip.de: 💡 Deutsch sagt *früher* und die Vergangenheit, Englisch **used to** + Grundform.
tip.it: 💡 L'italiano dice l'imperfetto (*abitavo*), l'inglese **used to** + la forma base: **I used to live**.
tip.en: 💡 Only the past: there is no *I use to* for now. After **did** it's **use**.
